text:
nina: throwing a sketch out: "micro-compaction" for hot byte-ranges inside big shards to reduce fragmentation and avoid full-shard evictions
lee: short: sample ranges, group hot ones, relocate to contiguous slots so eviction doesn't scatter them?
omar: how do you sample without heavy overhead?
nina: cheap: 1B probabilistic hits per access, saturating 2-bit counter per 64KB range by default. aggregator runs per-minute and emits hot-range sets.
lee: relocation path? sync vs async?
nina: prefer compact-on-write: on write to a cold range we attempt to pull neighboring hot ranges into a staging area and remap atomically. two modes: quick-sync (bounded ms) or enqueue async worker if budget missed.
omar: atomic remap concerns for pointer stability and KV refs? race window must be tiny.
nina: we use publish-with-epoch semantics: write staging copy, publish new descriptor entry, wait epoch drain then free old pages. serves are always looking at descriptor+epoch.
lee: staging capacity — do we need big pools? noisy neighbors?
nina: small ephemeral per-node staging (config default 2-4% mem) tagged by tenant/priority. fallback is to reuse host-staging with tenant tags. credits system prevents one tenant blasting compaction.
omar: eviction interplay — might re-evict freshly compacted pages.
nina: sampler weights feed into eviction score; compacted clusters get boosted locality score so they stay longer. also batch compactions to avoid ping-pong.
lee: failure modes? mid-remap crash?
nina: publish step is the single point: until publish, nothing visible. after publish, free is background and idempotent. compactor writes a small journal for recovery.
omar: metrics to surface?
lee: compaction_ops, avg_sync_ms, staged_bytes, p95 cold-write-latency, compaction_credit_balance per-tenant.
infra-bot: created issue RUNTIME-2134: "micro-compaction (hot-range sampler + compact-on-write) PoC" and linked this thread. :robot_face:
nina: plan: telemetry-only first (collect hotset patterns 2 weeks), enable for opt-in tenants with strict budgets, then ramp. who wants to pair on PoC?
omar: I can help on allocator remap bits.
lee: I'll sketch the eviction weight changes.
nina: thanks — will open an initial patch with a minimal sampler and telemetry endpoint later today.
